semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الملك}: this is the reading of the majority, I mean the genitive «الملِكِ», with what follows it as a naʿt (adjective) of it; a badal (substitute) is weak because of their being derived forms. Abū Wāʾil, Maslama ibn Muḥārib and Ruʾba read it with the nominative ending, with an implied mubtadaʾ requiring praise. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And if it were read in the accusative, on the pattern of their saying «الحمدُ الله أهلَ الحَمْد», that would be a possible reading." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «القَدُّوس» with fatḥa on the qāf. The discussion of it, and of «الأمِّيِّ» and its plural «الأمِّيِّين», has already been given. And «يَتْلُوا» and what follows are ṣifas (qualifiers) of «رسول».

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {وَآخَرِينَ}: there are two possibilities. The first is that it is genitive by ʿaṭf (conjunction) on «الأمِّيِّيْنَ», that is: "and He sent among others of the unlettered." And {لَمَّا يَلْحَقُواْ بِهِمْ} is a ṣifa of the preceding «آخرين». The second is that it is accusative by ʿaṭf on the accusative pronoun in «يُعَلِّمُهم», that is: "and He teaches others who have not yet joined them, but will join them." Everyone who learns the law of Muḥammad ﷺ until the end of time has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as his teacher in potentiality (bi-l-quwwa), because he is the source of that great good and weighty virtue.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {حُمِّلُواْ التوراة}: this is the reading of the majority. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «حَمَلوا», lightened, in the active.
His saying {كَمَثَلِ الحمار}: this is the reading of the majority. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «حِمارٍ» indefinite. It is equivalent in force to the reading of the others, because by «الحمار» the genus is meant. For this reason it was qualified by the clause after it, as will come. Al-Maʾmūn ibn Hārūn al-Rashīd read «يُحَمَّلُ» with shadda, in the passive. The clause «يَحْمِلُ» or «يُحْمَّلُ» has two possibilities: the first, which is the well-known one, is that it is in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الحمار»; the second is that it is in the position of a ṣifa (qualifier) for «الحمار», because it behaves like an indefinite, since the genus is meant by it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "or genitive as a qualifier, because «الحمار» is like «اللئيم» in his saying:
4261 - ولَقد أَمُرُّ على اللئيمِ يَسُبُّني ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And indeed I pass by the base man who curses me...)
This has been set out already, and that from it, in the view of some, is {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الليل نَسْلَخُ} [Yā Sīn: 37], and that «نَسْلَخُ» is a naʿt of «الليل». The majority make it a ḥāl because of the formal definiteness. As for the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, the clause is only a qualifier, and it is not impossible, in the view of Sībawayh, that it be a ḥāl.
الأَسْفار is the plural of سِفْر, which is a book of gathered leaves.
His saying {بِئْسَ مَثَلُ القوم}: there are several possibilities. The first, which is the apparent and well-known one, is that «مَثَلُ القوم» is the agent of «بِئْس». And the one specified for blame is the relative noun after it. That poses a difficulty, because there must be agreement in reference between the agent of niʿma and biʾsa and the one specified, and here the "likeness" is not the denying people. The answer is that there is an omitted muḍāf, that is: بِئْسَ مَثَلُ القومِ مَثَلُ الذين كَذَّبوا. The second is that «الذين» is a ṣifa of «القوم», so that it is genitive in position, and the one specified for blame is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being: "evil is the likeness of the denying people, the likeness of these"; and this is close to the first. The third is that the agent is omitted, and that «مَثَلُ القومِ» is the one specified for blame, its implied form being: بِئْسَ المَثَلُ مَثَلُ القوم, with the relative noun again a naʿt of «القوم». Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words incline to this, for he said: "The implied form is: بِئْسَ المَثَلُ مَثَلُ القومِ." This is invalid, because the agent is not omitted in the view of the Basrans except in three places, of which this is not one, unless one adopts the view of the Kufans. The fourth is that the tamyīz (specification) is omitted and the agent that it explains is latent, its implied form being: بئس مَثَلاً مَثَلُ القوم. Al-Zamakhsharī's words incline to this, for he said: "«بئْسَ مَثَلاً مَثَلُ القوم»", so that the agent is latent, explained by «مَثَلاً», and «مَثَلُ القومِ» is the one specified for blame, the relative noun being a ṣifa of it, and the tamyīz omitted. Sībawayh and his followers do not permit this at all; they stated explicitly that omitting the tamyīz is impermissible, and how could it be omitted when it is what clarifies?

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ}: it stands in the place of the two objects, or the one object, depending on the disagreement. And «لله» is attached to «أَوْلياء», or to an omitted element as a naʿt of «أولياء»; and {مِن دُونِ الناس} likewise.
And His saying {فَتَمَنَّوُاْ الموت} is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The majority read it with ḍamma on the wāw, which is the original for the wāw of the pronoun. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ, Ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with kasra, which is the original in the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ also read it with fatḥa, which is a seeking of lightness, and the like of it was given in His saying {اشتروا الضلالة} [al-Baqara: 16]. Al-Kisāʾī reported the substitution of a hamza for the wāw.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يَتَمَنَّونَهُ}: and He said in [Sūrat] al-Baqara «ولن يتمنَّوْه». Al-Zamakhsharī [spelled in the source "al-Zamshkhasharī"] said: "There is no difference between «لا» and «لن» in that each of them is a negation of the future, except that «لن» contains an emphasis and intensity that «لا» does not; so once He used the wording of emphasis, «ولن يتمنَّوْه», and once without its wording, «ولا يتمنَّوْنه»." The Shaykh said: "This is a retraction on his part of his position, namely that «لن» requires negation in perpetuity, in favour of the position of the group, namely that it does not require it." I say: there is no retraction in it; the most that can be said is that he was silent about it. His joining «لا» and «لن» in negating the future does not rule out «لن» being distinguished by another meaning. This discussion has already been given more fully in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {فَإِنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُمْ}: there are two possibilities regarding the fāʾ. The first is that it enters because of the sense of condition (sharṭ) that the noun implies, and the ruling for what is described by a relative noun is the ruling for the relative noun in that respect. The second is that it is purely redundant (mazīda), not for the implication mentioned. These people invalidated the first view on two grounds. One is that this is permissible only when the mubtadaʾ or the noun of «إنَّ» is a relative noun, and the noun of «إنَّ» here is not a relative noun but is described by a relative noun. The other is that fleeing from death does not save from it, so it does not resemble a condition; he means that it is certain, so it does not resemble the condition, whose nature is to be uncertain.
The first was answered by saying that what is described, together with its description, is like one thing, and that «الذي» is only ever a qualifier; so when the thing described is not mentioned the fāʾ enters, the described being intended, and likewise when it is stated explicitly. The second was answered by saying that a great many people suppose that fleeing from the causes of death will save them till another time. Makkī allowed that the khabar be His saying {الذي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ}, with the fāʾ introducing the answer to the clause. He said: "As you say: «زيدٌ منطلقٌ فقُمْ إليه»." There is room for objection, because there is no sequence between His saying {إِنَّ المَوْتَ الذي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ} and His saying {فَإِنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُمْ}, so it is not a parallel to what he gave as example.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إنه» without a fāʾ, and there are several possibilities concerning it. The first is that it is resumptive, and then the khabar is the relative noun itself, as if it were said: "Death is the thing that you flee from"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second is that the khabar is the clause «إنَّه مُلاقيكم», and then the relative noun is a naʿt of «الموت». The third is that «إنَّه» is an emphasis; since the speech about death became long, the particle was emphasized with verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī). You know that it is emphasized in this way only by repeating what it governed, or by repeating its pronoun; so it was emphasized by repeating the pronoun of what «إنَّ» had entered. Then the relative noun is a naʿt of «الموت», and «مُلاقِيكم» is its khabar, as if it were said: «إنَّ الموتَ إنَّه مُلاقيكم».

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {مِن يَوْمِ الجمعة}: this «مِنْ» is a clarification (bayān) of «إذا» and an explanation of it; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: it is in the sense of «في», that is, "on the day". The majority read «الجمعة» with two ḍammas. Ibn al-Zubayr, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Ḥaywa and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read it with sukūn on the mīm. It was said: it is a dialectal variant of the first and was made quiescent for lightness, being the dialect of Tamīm. It was also said: it is a maṣdar in the sense of gathering (ijtimāʿ). It was also said: since it is in the sense of the act, it became like رجل هُزْأَة, that is, a man who is mocked; so when al-jumʿa has the sense of gathering, it was made quiescent, because it is a direct object in meaning, or resembles it, and so it became like هُزْأَة, he who is mocked. Makkī said this; Abū l-Baqāʾ likewise said: "It is in the sense of 'that in which people gather', like رجل ضُحْكَة, that is, one who is laughed at." Makkī said: "Making the mīm quiescent is permissible for lightness. It was also said that it is a dialect." I say: it has been given that it is a reading, and that it is the dialect of Tamīm. The Shaykh said: "There is also a dialect with fatḥa which has not been read." I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ reported it as a reading, saying: "It is read with fatḥa on the mīm in the sense of the agent, that is, the day of the place that gathers, like رجلٌ ضُحْكَة, that is, one who laughs much." Makkī said something close to it, for he said: "And there is a third dialect with fatḥa on the mīm, attributing the act to it, as if it gathers the people, as one says رجلٌ لُحَنَة if he often corrects people's grammar, and قُرَأَة if he often teaches people to recite." Al-Zamakhsharī also reported it as a reading, except that he made «الجُمْعة» with sukūn the original and the one with ḍamma a lightened form of it [as written]; he said: "يوم الجُمعة is the day of the gathered crowd, like their saying ضُحْكَة for one laughed at. And يوم الجُمعة with fatḥa on the mīm is the day of the time that gathers, like their saying ضُحَكة and لُعَبة; and يوم الجُمُعة is a heavier form of الجُمْعَة, as عُسُرة was said for عُسْرة. And it has been read with all of them." [Translator's note: the text as printed describes the ḍamma form as "lightened" and then the heavier form as a thickening; it is translated as written.] His implied form "the day of the time that gathers" is better than Abū l-Baqāʾ's "the day of the place that gathers", because attributing gathering to the two adverbials is figurative, so it is preferable to keep it as time, in its state.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {انفضوا إِلَيْهَا}: He returned the pronoun to the commerce rather than the diversion, because it is the more important of the cause. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He said «إليها» and did not say «إليهما» out of concern for the more important, since it was the cause of the diversion, and the diversion was not its cause. And consider that commerce was put before diversion in the sighting because it is more important, and was put after it in the preference, so that the soul first lights upon the clearer." End. In his saying "He did not say «إليهما»" and then answering as he did there is an objection that is not hidden; for with a conjunction by «أو» the pronoun, the khabar, the ḥāl and the qualifier are not put in the dual, because it is for one of the two things; for that reason people interpreted «إنْ يكُنْ غنياً أو فقيراً فاللَّهُ أَوْلى بهما» as I set out in its place. The answer to it is only that He put the pronoun in the singular because the conjunction is by «أو». And the pronoun of the commerce was brought, rather than the pronoun of the diversion, though the latter would be permissible, for what Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned in answer, which is the fact of its being the more important, as more than one has said. Al-Zamakhsharī too said something close to what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, for he said: "How did He say «إليها» when He has mentioned two things? I say: its implied form is: when they saw commerce they dispersed to it, or a diversion they dispersed to it; so one was omitted because the mentioned one indicates it, and likewise the reading of those who read «انفَضُّوا إليه»." End. His saying "I say: its implied form..." to the end suggests that the proper form of the speech was that the pronoun be dual, but it was omitted. In it is what I set before you: that what prevents this is a technical matter, namely the conjunction by «أو».
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «إليه», returning the pronoun to the diversion; al-Akhfash expressly allowed that on the basis of hearing it from the Arabs, for example: «إذا جاءك زيد أو هند فأَكْرِمه», and if you wish «فأكرِمْها». Some read «إليهما» in the dual. Its explanation is like the explanation of {إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقِيراً} [al-Nisāʾ: 135], whose treatment has been given.
His saying: {وَتَرَكُوكَ}: a circumstantial clause from the agent of «انفَضُّوا», with «قد» implied in the view of some. And His saying {مَا عِندَ الله خَيْرٌ}: «ما» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and «خيرٌ» is its khabar.
